kpis.label: Reference price
kpis.sub: Rs 131.69 = FY26 basic EPS of Rs 5.64 x 23.35, the lowest peer P/E in the DRHP's own table (Escorts Kubota, p. 156). It is a reference point for sizing the model, not a price band and not a view of fair price. The only priced transaction in the DRHP is the 22-Oct-2025 allotment to the promoters at Rs 1,547 per Rs 10 share, Rs 33.63 after the bonus and split, for the business transfer (p. 163).

focus.title: Customer / supplier / geographic concentration
focus.detail: Threshold test (above 80%): Northern and Central states were 93.99% of FY26 revenue (Punjab 25.79%, Haryana 18.48%, p. 56). Top customer Seth Agro Industries 25.21% of FY26 revenue (17.20% in FY25); top-10 customers 50.04%. Super Seeder and Straw Reaper together 59.06% of FY26 revenue (p. 26). Supplier concentration is disclosed only for FY25 and FY24 (top-1 was the promoter proprietorship SMW II at 52.55% and 44.13% of expenses), not for FY26; the DRHP says no long-term supply agreement terms are disclosed in the table.

focus.title: Cash flow vs profit
focus.detail: Cash flow statement is present. CFO 12.49 / 13.02 / 2.69 Rs cr (FY24 / FY25 / FY26); cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7% (281.93 / 404.39 Rs m), FY26 alone 8.6%. Cash generated from operations was Rs 131.36 m before Rs 104.52 m tax. FY26 working capital absorbed inventory Rs 445.46 m and other assets Rs 281.35 m. The FY26 receivables line shows a Rs 242.66 m decrease although closing receivables (Rs 612.95 m) exceed the FY25 standalone balance (Rs 244.72 m); the acquired opening balances are not shown separately in the statement.

focus.title: Related-party capex & subsidiaries
focus.detail: No related-party capex in FY26 (last: Rs 2.60 m from Goodfield Technology in FY24). Two other related-party points: (i) the Dehlon site for the Rs 716.64 m capex object is leased to the company by promoter Jagatjit Singh (rent Rs 1.01 m in FY26); (ii) Rs 45.00 m of loans/advances to Jagatjit Singh were outstanding at 31-Mar-2026 and Rs 10.00 m was advanced to Dharam Singh in FY26 (p. 95). The subsidiary Jagatjit Energies was bought for Rs 0.1 m on 30-Dec-2025 and receives no proceeds under the objects.

focus.title: Goodwill vs tangible equity
focus.detail: Goodwill Rs 4.55 m (0.6% of equity) in the restated consolidated balance sheet. The proforma balance sheet shows goodwill of Rs 65.66 m at FY25 and a capital reserve of Rs 32.98 m at FY24, so the purchase-accounting treatment differs between the restated and proforma statements; the DRHP does not reconcile them.

focus.title: Auditor qualifications / changes
focus.detail: No qualification on the numbers. Auditor history: Singla Gupta & Co resigned 23-Apr-2024 (stated reason: preoccupation); Kansal Sandeep & Associates was appointed 02-May-2024 for FY24 only and ceased 30-Sep-2024 on completion of tenure; Anup Kumar Jain & Co appointed 30-Sep-2024 (peer review certificate 016161; the two earlier firms are shown without one). FY25 and FY24 statements are special-purpose Ind AS statements restated under ICDR. Promoters Jagatjit Singh and Dharam Singh were disqualified as directors 01-Nov-2016 to 31-Oct-2021 (a former group company struck off); a compounding application is pending (p. 36).

focus.title: CARO / audit trail
focus.detail: CARO / Rule 11(g): the accounting software had no database-level audit trail up to 31-Dec-2025 (FY26) and for all of FY25; the company says it was enabled in January 2026. No adjustment to the restated numbers.

focus.title: Lead-manager track record
focus.detail: The DRHP lists only two IPOs handled by Keynote Financial Services in the period: Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (Exports), Apr-2026, -23.53% at day 30 and -15.98% at day 90 against issue price; CSM Technologies, Jul-2026, -2.75% at day 30. Neither has a 180-day reading. Both are in data/merchant_bankers.json. The full BRLM track record is delegated to the BRLM's website.

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -42.3% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: Price band, offer expenses, GCP amount and post-issue share count (all [●])

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: Interim financials: audited record ends 31-Mar-2026 (178 days before the DRHP date); the FY26 peak-season (Oct-Jan) inventory unwind and receipts after year-end are not shown

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: FY26 supplier concentration (only FY25 and FY24 given) and the identity and relationship of the largest FY26 customer, Seth Agro Industries (25.21%)

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Purchase accounting for the business transfer: goodwill Rs 4.55 m (restated) versus Rs 65.66 m (proforma FY25); fair-value allocation of the Rs 324.57 m consideration

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Weighted average cost of the promoter issue: DRHP prints Rs 35.15 per share (p. 163) but Rs 324.57 m / 9,650,984 shares = Rs 33.63 (Rs 1,547 / 46). The difference is not explained

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Capex object: no orders placed; quotations valid 9 months to 1 year; Dehlon land is leased from a promoter (lease term and rent not tested against market)

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Only three listed peers, none with a comparable portfolio (issuer's own statement, p. 156); relative valuation rests on tractor and tiller makers

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Current price and 3-year financials of Keynote's two listed IPOs (merchant banker table)

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Subsidy receivables: state subsidy payment delays are a stated risk (p. 56); amount outstanding and ageing by scheme are not given

comfort.title: Bonus issue / share-count consistency
comfort.detail: 22:1 bonus (board 27-May-2026) and 1:2 split (EGM 04-May-2026) are applied retrospectively: EPS 5.64 / 1.42 / 0.57 and NAV 12.75 / 1.54 / 0.12 are on the restated count. The share count behind each year differs: FY26 uses 55,650,984 shares (313.90 / 5.64), FY25 and FY24 use about 46.1 m and 43.9 m (the pre-allotment count), because 9,650,984 shares were issued to the promoters on 22-Oct-2025 for the business transfer. FY26 EPS divides by the full post-issue count, not a time-weighted count; we have not re-weighted it.

comfort.title: Current vs deferred tax
comfort.detail: Current tax Rs 130.30 m of a Rs 130.21 m FY26 charge (deferred credit Rs 0.09 m). Cumulative current tax is 26.1% of cumulative PBT (147.09 / 562.64 Rs m) against a 25.17% statutory rate, so profit is struck after tax that has been paid.

comfort.title: Revaluation reserve
comfort.detail: No revaluation reserve in other equity; the company states it has not issued shares out of revaluation reserve.

comfort.title: Contingent liabilities
comfort.detail: Contingent liabilities Rs 71.70 m (income tax 0.18; GST 22.67, of which Rs 2.14 m relates to SMW I and is to be borne by the company under the BTA; other 6.50; bank guarantees 42.35) = 10.1% of equity of Rs 709.29 m.

comfort.title: Monitoring agency
comfort.detail: Monitoring agency to be appointed (issue above Rs 1,000 m). Rs 185 m of proceeds repays bank borrowings of Rs 1,641.44 m outstanding at 31-Aug-2026; Rs 1,340.89 m is secured by promoters' personal guarantees (p. 40), so repayment may release some of them: an indirect promoter benefit. The related-party loans from promoters (Rs 2.29 m + 0.89 m + 4.83 m) are not listed for repayment.

comfort.title: Eligibility re-computation
comfort.detail: Re-performed: the issuer states it does not meet Reg 6(1)(a) or 6(1)(c) and offers under Reg 6(2) (at least 75% to QIBs). Net tangible assets 704.75 / 70.78 / 5.32 Rs m and monetary assets 161.59 / 39.14 / 33.26 Rs m (22.9% / 55.3% / 625% of NTA) at FY26 / FY25 / FY24: the FY24 net worth of Rs 5.32 m is below the Rs 10 m test and FY25 monetary assets exceed 50%. The statement reproduces from the balance sheets. KPI EBITDA 557.38 reproduces from the P&L (444.12 + 101.63 + 46.66 - 35.03).

comfort.title: SME conditions
comfort.detail: Offer for sale up to 3,100,000 shares by Jagatjit Singh, 6.3% of his 48,990,736 shares (below half of his holding). At the Rs 131.69 reference the OFS is Rs 408.2 m, 12.0% of a Rs 3,408.2 m offer (under the 20% ceiling). Re-test at the RHP price.

bankers.name: Keynote Financial Services Limited
bankers.owner: Promoter holding reported at about 71.9% (promoters include Vivek Suchanti, 10.45% after a June-2025 HUF partition)

issues.sector: Basmati rice and agri-commodity exports (per secondary reports)

strengths: Proforma revenue Rs 2,074.48 m / 2,537.60 m / 4,139.70 m FY24-FY26, a 41.3% two-year CAGR (p. 158)
ROCE 31.10% and ROE 53.89% in FY26; interest cover 5.03x (p. 158)
Cash tax 26.1% of cumulative PBT, above the 25.17% statutory rate (p. 87)
233 dealers and 12 distributors in 20 states, up from 15 states in FY25; 192 SKUs (pp. 158, 247)
Both plants run at 73.62% (Cheema) and 89.68% (Dehlon) utilisation in FY26 (p. 266)
weaknesses: Operating cash flow Rs 26.85 m against PAT Rs 313.90 m in FY26; cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7% (p. 88)
Seth Agro Industries 25.21% and top-10 customers 50.04% of FY26 revenue (p. 261)
Super Seeder 32.99% and Straw Reaper 26.07% of FY26 revenue (p. 26)
Debt/equity 1.89x; borrowings Rs 1,344.07 m, of which Rs 1,340.89 m carry promoter personal guarantees (pp. 40, 158)
Audit trail not enabled at database level until Jan-2026 (p. 52)
opportunities: Soil-preparation equipment forecast to grow at 10.2% CAGR FY26-FY30, issuer-commissioned CARE report (p. 209)
Dehlon capacity to rise from 4,000 to 33,000 units with the Rs 716.64 m object (p. 137)
Entry into briquette and pellet machinery (p. 261)
Export revenue only 1.36% of FY26, so the base is small if exports recover (p. 158)
threats: Demand linked to CRM and SMAM subsidies, with past payment delays by state governments (p. 56)
Northern and Central states 93.99% of revenue; Punjab 25.79%, Haryana 18.48% (p. 56)
Promoters ran competing businesses until 31-Mar-2025; non-compete runs 12 months after they cease control (p. 53)
Promoters were disqualified as directors 2016-2021; compounding application pending (p. 36)
Larger listed rivals: VST Tillers Tractors and Escorts Kubota (p. 156)
